title: Clinical implementation of an intensity-modulated technique for total body irradiation (TBI) at the Department of Radiation Therapy, University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein (UKSH), Kiel Campus
summary:
A central requirement of total body irradiation (TBI) is the uniform distribution of the radiation dose throughout the entire body. If medically necessary, the dose must also be reduced in radiation-sensitive areas such as the lungs.

With the previous technique, this uniform dose distribution is achieved through the use of a fixed compensator. This compensator is calculated based on your computed tomography (CT) images and placed in the radiation beam path to compensate for differences in body thickness and length.

In the new technique, this fixed compensator is replaced by an automatic, virtual compensation method known as intensity modulation. The radiation dose distribution and the treatment machine parameters (linear accelerator) are optimized using algorithms within a 3D treatment planning system, also based on your CT images, in accordance with the current state of the art in radiation therapy.

Dose measurements and the organizational aspects of treatment delivery are evaluated during routine treatment. Participation does not involve any additional therapeutic procedures or any changes to the medically prescribed treatment.

The aim of the study is to evaluate the technical feasibility, dosimetric quality, and organizational integration of the new TBI technique in routine clinical practice, as well as to identify opportunities for optimization for its future standard implementation.
conditions: Patients with hematologic diseases who have an indication for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. TBI is administered as part of the conditioning regimen.  The subject of the study is the evaluation of the routine implenetation of the irradiation technique; the underlying diseases themselves are not being investigated.

interventions.name:
Patients will receive the clinically indicated TBI as part of the conditioning regimen prior to hematopoietic stem cell transplantation using a newly implemented combined VMAT/IMRT technique.

No additional therapeutic interventions will be performed as part of the study.

Inclusion criteria:
Planned TBI as part of a conditioning regimen prior to hematopoietic stem cell transplantation at the University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein (UKSH), Kiel Campus
